newsitem.title: GERMANY: Issing says M3 growth slowed in March.
newsitem.headline: Issing says M3 growth slowed in March.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Thursday he expected M3 money supply growth to have slowed in March, continuing a two-month tendency.
Issing also said the government's projected 1997 economic growth rate of 2.5 percent was realistic.
At the same time, Issing said that rising import prices was a negative factor.
The Bundesbank will likely release its March M3 data in the next days and independent economists forecast a rate of around 8.5 percent after February's 9.1 percent headline rate.
They say monetary capital formation continued to pick up even though private sector lending is expected to have remained strong.
Issing was speaking at a news conference following a regular policy-setting council meeting.
Import prices have in recent months been boosted by the mark's depreciation on currency markets.
